answer: Plants rely on gravity only once they are tall, and until then they recognize the direction of gravity by the pattern of light hitting their leaves, so a seedling can sense which side is light and germinate accordingly. Vascular bundles, the columns running up a stem, also detect gravity because they change shape when pulled from one side an inch. Once a plant is the orach height, it rarely reorients itself; instead, the growth hormones—all developed one at a time in a single burst—now control the plant’s vertical orientation for good.
